summary.value: The Easter Egger is not a true breed but an American hatchery mix. It comes from crossing a bird that carries the blue egg gene with a brown egg layer, so no poultry standard covers it, and it is sometimes sold as "Americana", which is a different thing from the Ameraucana breed. Birds come in any color, and many have muffs, beards and a small pea comb. Their legs may be gray, yellow or greenish. The big draw is the eggs: shells may be blue, green, olive, brown or even pinkish, and each hen keeps the same shade for life. Hens lay about 200 to 280 medium to large eggs a year and seldom go broody. They are friendly, docile and curious, cope with both hot and cold weather, and make an easy choice for beginners and families.
